$comment: Settings for npm run produce. Numbers marked 'bible' come from docs/bible; change them there first. A run records the limits it used in production/state.json, and the pull request says when they were not these defaults.

limits.$comment: Ceilings only, never a target: there is no minimum length, and the first rule (bible 00, Article 1: only include it if it's interesting) decides how long an episode actually is. runtimeSeconds.max is the owner's ceiling ('aim for less than 10 minutes'): 590 s, just under ten minutes. words.max scales bible 10's 520 words for five minutes (300 s) to 590 s at the same rate (520 x 590 / 300, rounded down to 1020), inside bible 03's arithmetic of 1.6 to 2.2 spoken words per second of running time. wordsPerSecond: bible 03, runtime arithmetic. segmentTolerance: bible 10, stage 4. stories: outside this range is a warning, never a failure.

freshness.$comment: bible 03, fixed and fresh. History: each earlier published episode's production/plan.json, or its row in the rotation log in docs/bible/lore.md when it has no plan. One gate: the song's genre differs from the previous episode's. Everything else is a warning the plan may answer in 'overrides' (or a guest's 'repeatReason').

guestLines.$comment: The source comments a guest's line may carry (rule R3). realAccount: a puppet standing for a real account says only what that account published (the owner's rule: published content, essentially in its original context; no words put in their mouth), so pastiche is not here. invented: guests on .example. A verbatim line outside a thread must record its original occasion (the post it answered); whether the staged exchange recreates it is the reviewer's judgement. The guest-lines gate warns when realAccount differs from the tags R3 names.

pitchSections.$comment: The pitch's required sections are read from the template in docs/bible/10-process.md (stage 2). This list is used only if that template cannot be found, and the gate warns when it is.

frames.$comment: direct: frames are shot at every cue plus this many evenly spaced moments across each segment, at most maxPerSegment in all.

claude.$comment: The headless writer. model can be overridden with --model or PRODUCE_MODEL. Budgets are per writer call, in US dollars, enforced by Claude Code's --max-budget-usd (a client-side estimate).
